Calcium Carbonate

Understanding before selection.

Explore technical concepts ↓
01

What is calcium carbonate?

Calcium carbonate (CaCO₃) occurs naturally in limestone, chalk and marble. Its chemistry, mineral form and processing route influence how it behaves in an industrial formulation.

02

Ground or precipitated?

Ground calcium carbonate (GCC) is produced by mechanically processing natural carbonate rock. Precipitated calcium carbonate (PCC) is produced through a controlled chemical route. They differ in particle morphology and size distribution; selection depends on the application.

03

Coated or uncoated?

Surface treatment can change the interaction between mineral particles and a surrounding binder or polymer. Coated material may improve compatibility in selected systems; uncoated material remains relevant where the formulation requires an untreated mineral surface.

04

Consistency is an application question

Purity, particle distribution, moisture and dispersion should be considered together. A finer powder is not automatically a better choice. Material evaluation and formulation trials establish suitability.

CaCO₃ / APPLICATIONS

One mineral. Many applications.

Material selection begins with the formulation and the process—not a universal grade.

01

Plastics

Mineral fillers can influence stiffness, dimensional behavior and processing. Particle distribution, surface treatment and polymer compatibility guide selection.

02

Paints & coatings

Calcium carbonate acts as an extender and functional filler. Particle packing and dispersion affect the finish, while formulation determines the optical and rheological response.

03

Rubber

Filler choice influences compound processing and physical behavior. Evaluate dispersion, loading and compatibility with the elastomer and curing system.

04

Construction

Fine limestone fillers are used in mortars, renders and related building formulations. Grading, binder compatibility and workability are relevant selection factors.

05

Paper

Calcium carbonate is used as a filler and coating pigment. It can contribute to brightness, opacity and surface characteristics within a suitable papermaking system.

06

Adhesives & sealants

Mineral fillers help shape body and flow. Particle size, moisture and surface chemistry must be matched to the binder and application method.

CaCO₃ / TECHNICAL INFORMATION

The details that define a material.

Technical concepts for a more informed material selection discussion.

01Particle size & distribution+

A distribution describes a range of sizes. Median size alone does not capture coarse particles or the full spread. Compare results obtained with compatible test methods.

02Purity+

Chemical composition and accessory minerals affect suitability. Request relevant analytical information for the intended use.

03Whiteness & brightness+

Optical properties are measured under defined conditions. Whiteness and brightness are related but distinct; compare the method as well as the result.

04Moisture+

Moisture can influence flow, dispersion and moisture-sensitive formulations. Storage and handling conditions are part of the assessment.

05Surface treatment+

The treatment type and its compatibility with the binder or polymer matter. Coated and uncoated grades should be evaluated for the specific formulation.

06Fineness+

Fineness may be described through particle size or sieve residue. A meaningful comparison needs a stated measurement method.

07Packaging & handling+

Discuss packaging format, contamination prevention, storage conditions and handling requirements directly. No packaging format is assumed.

Industrial materials & solutions · Saudi Arabia

Calcium carbonate for Saudi industry

For manufacturers in Saudi Arabia, the useful question is how a mineral fits the application: polymer processing, coating formulation, construction materials or paper. Discuss the intended use, required documentation and handling conditions before selecting a material.
